title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
lede: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen is a fast model for everyday coding and agent work that replaces 3.8 Flash across the Gemini app, Search, the Gemini API and Antigravity.

points: Google says it scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at default settings, above Gemini 4 Argon's 50.
Pricing is flat across a 1 million-token context: $1.50 per million input and $7.50 per million output tokens.
Against 3.8 Flash it finishes tasks 2.5 times faster and scores 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1, up from 18.2%.
Four thinking levels run from low up to a new xhigh tier.
It is meant to pair with Carbon and Argon, and Antigravity's new Orchestrator switches between them mid-session.

points.text: The element names confuse people: commenters cannot tell how Hydrogen ranks against Argon or Carbon.
Price is the main complaint: Hydrogen costs as much as list-price 3.8 Flash, with no cheap lite tier, and one team says it may migrate away.
Some expect a near-frontier free default to lift public perception of AI; a reply says small models shine on benchmarks but disappoint in real use.
One tester rates its image-to-HTML output between Sonnet and Opus, roughly level with GPT Sol.
